newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania miners' strikes spread to new regions.
newsitem.headline: Romania miners' strikes spread to new regions.

text.p: Strikes by Romanian miners demanding higher pay and safeguards against government market reforms spread to two new coalfields on Monday, with pit workers blocking the country's main north-south highway.
It was unclear how many miners were on strike. It appeared from media reports to be a minority of the 100,000 employed in the largely loss-making sector throughout the country.
The state news agency Rompres said 3,000 miners in the western Banat coalfield, near the border with Yugoslavia, had stopped work to press demands for tax cuts.

Hundreds more launched a strike in Prahova, dragging trucks and bulldozers across the main highway linking Bucharest and the oil refining centre of Ploiesti. Police re-routed traffic down minor roads.
Striking miners in the Bihor region, near the Hungarian border, were staging marches in several towns.

The most militant miners in western Romania's Jiu Valley walked off the job last week demanding a 45 percent pay rise. They also want the release of trade union boss Miron Cosma, standing trial on charges of undermining the state.
Cosma is alleged to have led a rampage through Bucharest in September 1991 which ultimately toppled the country's first post-communist government.
Miners take home monthly pay of more than $100, compared to average wages of about $80. They also have communist-era privileges like rent, electricity and transport discounts.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and ministers in his centrist coalition government were to meet miners later in the day.
The centrists, who ousted ex-communists in elections last November, are pressing ahead with tough reforms, including the closure of loss-making industries, such as mining.
